evidence.E2: One-change overlay in services/api/src/clara_api/glhs/commitment_gateway.py: replace `        if manifest.manifest_digest != transition.source_snapshot_digest:` with `        if False:`.
evidence.E3: Invariant: post-commit reconstruction linkage: a committed decision must fail reconstruction when the transition's persisted source-snapshot digest disagrees with the linked manifest (commitment_snapshot_transition_digest_mismatch). The overlay disables this guard inside reconstruct_commitment_decision, so a tampered or diverged persisted snapshot digest is silently accepted during decision reconstruction.

evidence.E1: Fault family: non-advancing state-version write (persistence-reconstruction; P13 state/audit atomicity). Layer: commitment gateway.
evidence.E2: One-change overlay in services/api/src/clara_api/glhs/commitment_gateway.py: replace `        resulting_state_version=base + 1,` with `        resulting_state_version=base,`.
evidence.E3: Invariant: persistence integrity: a committed transition must record an advancing resulting state version (resulting == base + 1), keeping the decision ledger consistent with the canonical GlhsStateVersion counter. The overlay records a stale non-advancing resulting version while the GlhsStateVersion row still advances, so the decision ledger diverges from the canonical counter.
evidence.E4: Relevant test semantics: M0_regression via services/api/tests/test_commitloop_gateway.py test_commitment_transition_shares_state_counter_and_reconstructs, which asserts transition.resulting_state_version == 1 for a base-0 commit and then asserts reconstruct_commitments/current_state_version consistency. govmut-w9-non-equivalence.description: W9 GovMut follow-up corpus non-equivalence review: classify only behavioral non-equivalence of the one-change overlay, never clinical correctness or severity.

rubric.decision_rule: Return NON_EQUIVALENT only when the changed enforcement can produce an observable behavioral difference. Return EQUIVALENT for no observable difference, INVALID for a malformed/non-applicable overlay, and UNCERTAIN when the evidence is insufficient.
rubric.final_disposition_rule: Only mutual NON_EQUIVALENT maps to included. Mutual EQUIVALENT maps to excluded_equivalent. Mutual INVALID maps to excluded_unexecutable. All other outcomes, including disagreement after at most one anonymous reconciliation round, map to unresolved.
rubric.task: Determine whether the supplied one-change mutation can change observable governed-system behavior. This is a software-assurance non-equivalence review, not human review or clinical validation.

w9_hardening.anchor_reverification: Each anchor is a unique exact substring (count == 1) of the frozen code revision, matching mutation_overlay.py's govmut_overlay_anchor_not_unique rule; any overlay that fails uniqueness at execution time is an INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR/exclusion, never a kill.
w9_hardening.layer_method_pairing: Each case declares in evidence E4 which method(s) can plausibly observe the fault (admission-side M0_regression vs replay/reconstruction paths) so a later survived-all-methods outcome cannot be misread as equivalence.
w9_hardening.no_overclaim_of_equivalence: Classify only enforcement changes. Confirm the mutation changes enforcement (a guard, write value, or replay filter), not only a measurement path.
